answer: Tail-value sybil resistance uses a basalt-hard collateral bond pooled like catastrophe reserves, where each identity posts capital sized to a 1-in-200-year correlated loss event. Membership spreads along a vine of co-signed attestations, so a fake cluster must fund every linked node, multiplying attacker cost by cluster size. A river of correlated slashing then fires when any node defects, pricing sybils out but leaving residual risk if attackers accept correlated loss.
